title: The Weight of the Handle (የእጁ ሚስጥር)
story_summary: A young highland farmer exhausts himself trying to break rocky soil with brute force alone. His grandfather quietly steps in—not with a lecture, but by adjusting his grip and rhythm—showing that balance and ancestral technique triumph over raw strain, embodying the Ethiopian proverb: 'የማያውቁት ነገር ላብ ያበረክታል'.
style_block: Cinematic photorealistic 35mm film still, authentic Ethiopian highland rural setting, natural earthy tones (ochre soil, weathered acacia wood, off-white handwoven cotton Gabi), subtle atmospheric dust, shallow depth of field, 24fps film grain, highly detailed skin textures and fabric weaves, centered composition suitable for 9:16 and 16:9 crops, no modern artifacts.

character_refs.kaleb: 17-year-old Ethiopian young man with short curly black hair, lean muscular build, dusty weathered beige linen tunic with rolled-up sleeves, worn brown leather sandals. Holding one single traditional Ethiopian agricultural tool (Doma): a straight weathered acacia wooden handle with a single pointed iron digging blade securely fitted at the end. No axe head, no double blades, no hammer, no extra tools.
character_refs.ato_berhanu: 70-year-old Ethiopian elder with a neatly trimmed silver-gray beard, deeply lined sun-weathered face, calm warm eyes, draped in a heavy off-white handwoven cotton Gabi with a subtle woven earth-toned border over a simple white cotton tunic.
